component.name: Kempt
component.summary: Tidy dnf and Flatpak updates for Fedora KDE

description.p: Kempt is a Plasma 6 widget and a command-line tool for dnf and Flatpak updates. It shows which updates are pending, leaves out the ones you hold, and installs them from the panel.
The count in the panel comes from the same cache the update uses. Updates published since that check can still join the update.

description.p: Kempt now says when a service stops starting after an update, and the widget's Startup Report lists what starts on its own. Put It Back restores a staged update that another program cancelled, and staging warns when Discover could cancel it. An update no longer hangs when a package's setup step restarts the service manager, and screen readers hear the whole widget.

A fix release. When another program changed your packages shortly after a check, an update or a stage, the widget could miss it. A dnf command run in a terminal cancels a staged update, and the widget went on saying the updates were staged until you pressed Refresh. It now checks within about a minute. kempt doctor also warns when getfacl is missing.

Updates now run inside the widget, with no terminal window. Before kernel, systemd and desktop updates, Kempt asks whether to install now or on the next restart. An install that used the terminal keeps it, and the widget offers the switch once. The widget can check its own installation, and it can turn off Discover's update notifier so you see one count. This release also fixes a security issue: the root helpers now set their own file permissions, so files root writes for dnf can no longer be left open to other users. On a computer that more than one account uses, run kempt doctor once after the upgrade. It finds files an older version left open and says how to fix each one.
